questions: When the board is fully visible, does it hold exactly three pens arranged in a single row?
Are all three pens aligned identically, all pointing the same way, including any pen near the left or right frame edge as it enters or exits?
Do all three pens share identical barrel and cap colors, with no mismatch?
Is every pen fully capped with no exposed writing tip, and are all three pens equal in length?
Does the board advance steadily from left to right at EVERY moment, never halting, freezing, or pausing even briefly (1-3 seconds) at any point in the video?
Do all pens stay fixed in their positions on the board, with no pen shifting, sliding, or moving on its own relative to the board mid-clip?

question_answers.evidence: When the board is fully in view (e.g., frames 12-16), there are clearly three pens visible on the white surface.
All three pens have their black caps pointing downwards and translucent barrels pointing upwards throughout the sequence.
All three pens appear to be identical black-capped pens with grey/translucent barrels.
All pens appear capped and of equal length.
The board moves steadily from left to right across the frames without stopping or reversing.

In frames 7-8, the three pens are relatively evenly spaced. However, from frame 9 onwards, the left-most pen has slid significantly closer to the middle pen, changing the spacing arrangement relative to the board.

parsed.reason: The pens change their relative spacing on the board mid-clip. Initially (frames 7-8), they are spaced apart, but then (frames 9-16) the left pen slides close to the middle pen, indicating they are not fixed in place.

description: Mid-clip, the pens themselves shift/move on their own due to an unseen external force; the board moves normally and no cause is visible in the scene.
